results.reasoning: Passes. The capture (as-built/cli/lint-focus-undeclared.html, scenario lint-focus-undeclared, fixture g2-focus-undeclared) prints the design's error line verbatim: a [storyboard] error on checkout.pay.card-declined naming the focus pay.decline-banner and both screens, pay or pay-error, with the declared anchors offered as a way out, then the failing summary and exit 1. The two differ only in fixture placeholders the designer flagged: the design types `walkdown lint` where the capture runs `--no-checks`, and the summary counts (4 rules vs 2). Not judged as faults. Beyond the drawing I drove the working tree's `walkdown lint` (node bin/walkdown.js, no server, no port used) against a throwaway blueprint under a mktemp HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME, nine rules in one feature (probe-lint-focus-cases.txt): a focus undeclared on two screens errors with the plural wording and a list cut at five 'and 2 more'; undeclared on one screen errors with the singular wording and lists that screen's anchors; a focus declared on the rule's second screen passes; a rule with no focus, with or without screens, is never asked for one; a screen declaring no anchors errors without an empty suggestion list; a rule naming no screens errors saying so; an anchor declared only on a screen the rule does not name is refused. Lint exits 1 with any of these and 0 (no focus error) with only the passing cases, with and without --no-checks. Edge, under 10% (a typo in `screens` on a rule that also sets focus): screens: [nope] gets the correct 'unknown screen' error plus a second, misleading 'the rule names no screen' focus error; the first error points at the fix, so it costs a moment's confusion. Named, not filed. Two shots were taken headless by a throwaway Playwright script over the two HTML files at 1280 wide.
